how_to_fill_this_out: Each entry is one rung of the ladder. Children go in "children", up to 5 levels in all (maker > brand > line > sub-line > sub-sub-line).
Array order is the order shown in the app's picker, most familiar first. Names you leave out are not lost: anything a person types is saved and appears after these.
name: spell it exactly as printed on the package. aliases: other spellings people use ("Purina Pro Plan"); they also match when a product is imported.
kind: manufacturer | brand | line | subline. A hint only; the depth, not the label, is what the app relies on.
species: omit when it is sold for every species. ["dog"] hides it from a cat owner's picker, ["cat"] hides it from a dog owner's.
tags: facet tags every product under this node inherits, e.g. ["diet:clinical"] on Prescription Diet.
verify: true marks a guess to check against a package or the maker's site. notes: anything the next editor should know.

Life stage (Kitten, Adult, Adult 7+, Senior, All Life Stages) is NOT a rung. It is a facet tag that rides with the product, because makers print it inside line names, product names or nowhere. Leave it out of the tree; a line name that is only a life stage is turned into a tag automatically. Use tags: ["life_stage:adult-7plus"] on a line that only ever holds one stage (Prime Plus).

Aliases are the safety net for rebrands and retailer spellings: any alias typed or imported lands on this node instead of creating a duplicate. Renaming a node in the app keeps the old name here automatically.
Seed it into the database with:  php artisan catalogue:seed-brands   (safe to repeat; fills gaps, never renames or moves anything).

children.name: Prime Plus
children.notes: Printed on the can as 'ADULT 7+ | PRIME PLUS'. The line is Prime Plus; Adult 7+ is carried as a life-stage tag, and retailers that swap the two still land here.
